title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 97
paragraphs: Having so decided, they began to put out to sea. They came past the temple of the “Revered Goddesses” to the Gaison and to Scolopoeis in Mycale, where there is a temple of Eleusinian Demeter, built by Philistos son of Pasicles when he accompanied Neileus son of Codros for the founding of Miletus. There they drew their ships up on shore and put an enclosure of stones and timber around them — cutting down fruit trees for the purpose — and fixed stakes around the enclosure, making preparations either to be besieged or to gain a victory; for in making their preparations they reckoned on both possibilities.
